Question: The set \(\{3,6,9,10\}\) is augmented by a fifth element \(n,\) not equal to any of the other four. The median of the resulting set is equal to its mean. What is the sum of all possible values of \(n?\)
Solution:
The original four numbers sum to \(28\), so the new mean is \((28+n)/5\). With five numbers, the median is the third number in increasing order. Its value depends on where \(n\) falls relative to \(6\) and \(9\).

If \(n<6\), the median is \(6\). Equality with the mean gives
\[
\frac{28+n}{5}=6,
\qquad n=2.
\]
If \(6<n<9\), the median is \(n\), so
\[
\frac{28+n}{5}=n,
\qquad 28=4n,
\qquad n=7.
\]
If \(n>9\), the median is \(9\), giving
\[
\frac{28+n}{5}=9,
\qquad n=17.
\]
The endpoints \(6\) and \(9\) are excluded by the question. These three cases cover every admissible value of \(n\), and \(2,7,17\) each lie in their required interval and avoid \(3,6,9,10\). Their sum is
\[
2+7+17=\boxed{26},
\]
choice E.
